posts.author: VEDANJANAM
posts.text:
Grahas and Dik (Directions)

In Jyotiṣa, each of the principal directions has a planetary lord. Varāhamihira enumerates these in the Bṛhajjātaka (2.5).

East: Sūrya
South-east: Śukra
South: Maṅgala
South-west: Rāhu
West: Śani
North-west: Candra
North: Budha
North-east: Guru

Ketu has no independent directional lordship in this classification.

This correspondence has practical applications in natal astrology, Praśna, Muhūrta and Vāstu.

The dignity, functional lordship, strength and afflictions of a graha provide the basis for assessing the suitability of its corresponding direction for a particular undertaking.

It is important to note that directional lordship and Digbala are distinct concepts. Maṅgala governs the south and attains maximum Digbala at the 10th bhāva madhya.

Directional lordship establishes the correspondence between a graha and physical space. Digbala measures the strength a graha derives from its position relative to the local horizon and meridian.
posts.my_take: Good one to keep handy .. directional lordship and digbala get mixed up all the time. Maṅgala rules the south but gets full digbala at the 10th bhāva madhya, two different things. The graha's dignity and lordship decide if its direction suits the work.

posts.author: VEDANJANAM
posts.text: @BikeridenWomen Rashi. Graha only if it has strong Dig Bala.
posts.my_take: Simple rule I like .. when picking a direction for something, go with the rāśi first, and use the graha's direction only when it has strong digbala. Clean and algorithmic, no guesswork.
